# wherdr v3 documentation

> wherdr is a web app to start coding agents on herdr-core (hc), follow their work and answer
> them from a phone. Read this index first, then only the section that answers your question.
> Links are relative to the repository root. A section that starts with "Needs:" makes sense only
> with the section it names: read that one too.

## Start here

- [Documentation home](docs/README.md): the list of pages, v3 and v2 only.
- [Overview](docs/overview.md#why-wherdr): what wherdr does for you.
- [How it works](docs/overview.md#how-it-works): wherdr's server, the hc socket, transcripts and the data folder.
- [herdr-core](docs/core.md): what v3 supports on hc, the reference for inventory, terminals and conversations.
- [First launch](docs/quick-start.md#quick-start): build, start and open wherdr, then the first settings.

## Install and update

- [Requirements](docs/installation.md#requirements): hc, Linux or macOS, Node.js 22 and Git.
- [Installation](docs/installation.md#installation): install v3 and run it as a service.
- [Keep it running](docs/installation.md#keep-it-running): run wherdr as a service (a systemd --user unit, a macOS LaunchAgent).
- [On-device dictation files](docs/installation.md#on-device-dictation-files): where the dictation models are fetched and kept.
- [Updating](docs/installation.md#updating): update v3 by hand; there is no update banner.
- [Install with an agent](docs/install-with-an-agent.md): ready-to-paste prompts for an agent that installs or updates wherdr.
- [Migrate from v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md): install v3 beside v2 and import its projects, machines and settings.
- [What is imported](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#what-is-imported): what the v2 import brings over, and what to redo.
- [Auto-deploy from a build machine](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#auto-deploy-from-a-build-machine): build elsewhere and deploy to the server.
- [Fall back to v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#fall-back-to-v2): go back to v2, and [uninstall v3](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#uninstall-v3).
- [Install as an app](docs/phone.md#install-it-as-an-app): add wherdr to a phone's home screen or a desktop browser.
- [App start](docs/phone.md#app-start): Settings › Phone › App start, network first or saved copy first.

## Network and security

- [Tailscale setup](docs/networks.md#recommended-always-on-server--tailscale): reach wherdr from a phone over a tailnet with HTTPS.
- [Other private networks](docs/networks.md#other-private-networks): Headscale, NetBird, ZeroTier or WireGuard instead.
- [Security](docs/security.md#security): who may reach wherdr, the passkey lock and remote-shell risks.
- [Network access](docs/security.md#network-access): which networks wherdr answers, and `WHERDR_TRUSTED_NETWORKS`.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md#configuration): environment variables and the data folder.

## Agent list

- [Agents on herdr-core](docs/home.md#agents-on-herdr-core): the live list, states, quick answers and the sidebar's order.
- [Alfred](docs/home.md#alfred): wherdr's assistant, its agent, home folder and memory.
- [Coordinators](docs/home.md#coordinators): project coordinator rows under Alfred and their menu.
- [Offered agents](docs/home.md#offered-agents): Settings › Agents, which programs every picker offers and in which order.
- [Machines as tabs](docs/home.md#machines-as-tabs): the machine bar, its groups and a machine's actions.
- [New agents and tabs](docs/home.md#new-agents-and-tabs): the New sheet and the + of a space's tabs.
- [Search](docs/home.md#search): search agents and conversations.
- [Inventory](docs/core.md#inventory): how terminals are placed in spaces and tabs, and how states are read.
- [Creating terminals and agents](docs/core.md#creating-terminals-and-agents-machines): what the New sheet asks hc to run.
- [Agent actions](docs/core.md#agent-actions): the agent's … menu: rename, keep after restart, answers, attachments.

## Conversation, terminal and files

- [Conversation and replies](docs/conversation.md): transcripts, one-tap answers, quoted replies, attachments and dictation.
- [Conversations on hc](docs/core.md#conversations): which agents open on their transcript and how it is read.
- [Terminal](docs/terminal.md): the real terminal, shared viewers and taking control.
- [Files](docs/files.md): browse an agent's folder, preview text, Markdown, images, PDFs and videos, download.
- [On a computer](docs/devices.md#on-a-computer): layout and keyboard shortcuts.
- [On a phone](docs/devices.md#on-a-phone): touch controls and the phone keybar.
- [On an iPad](docs/devices.md#on-an-ipad): the iPad layout.

## Project management

- [Getting started](docs/project-management.md#getting-started): the setup window, six steps from turning projects on to a first task; Finish setup on the board.
- [Projects](docs/project-management.md#projects): Settings › Projects, the project list and the project sheet's tabs.
- [General tab](docs/project-management.md#general): name, key, base (working) branch, agents, repository visibility, allowed machines and their clone paths (with a readiness check).
- [Workflow tab](docs/project-management.md#workflow): task types (with an optional weight) and steps, Edit as JSON, Save as template, Start over, review of the coordinator's proposed change (one-line summary, who proposed it, your full request with a link back to it, readable or JSON), and its card in the coordinator's conversation.
- [Guards](docs/project-management.md#guards): protected branches, who may merge (a waiting merge goes on once wherdr may do it; one you merge on GitHub ends as merged), contributor PRs, the project sheet's in-app addresses.
- [Automations](docs/project-management.md#automations): tasks added on a schedule or an event.
- [Template library](docs/project-management.md#template-library): saved templates and examples, read, rename and delete; projects keep their own copy.
- [Autopilot](docs/project-management.md#autopilot): the header button and its window, goal, wakes and limits.
- [Board](docs/project-management.md#board): columns (a done or archived task is never under Your turn), cards, time in the step and total time, Add task (with its weight: Auto, Light, Standard, Heavy), Start, Start on another machine (its readiness check), Stop, Delete.
- [Task sheet](docs/project-management.md#task-sheet): time per step, waits for you, review rounds and CI fixes, the task's buttons and its Description, Plan and Log tabs.
- [A task waiting for you](docs/project-management.md#a-task-waiting-for-you): the To do tab, Merge, Send back and other answers.
- [A stalled task](docs/project-management.md#a-stalled-task): red CI or an idle agent: the coordinator woken, one nudge, then Tasks to handle and a notification after 30 min.
- [Agents of a task that waits for you](docs/project-management.md#agents-of-a-task-that-waits-for-you): idle agents ended and started again.
- [Alfred's command](docs/alfred.md): `wherdr alfred`, what Alfred reads and changes after your yes (projects, their machines, guards, coordinators, settings).
- [After an update](docs/alfred.md#after-an-update): new instructions for Alfred and coordinators, and the one-line notice on their next command.

## Machines, quotas and notifications

- [Several machines](docs/machines.md#several-machines-ssh): machines reached by hc over SSH.
- [Before adding a machine](docs/machines.md#before-adding-a-machine): what a machine needs first.
- [Manage machines](docs/machines.md#manage-machines): Settings › Machines, add, reconnect, rename, forget, capacity (memory, cores, load on Linux and macOS) and memory limits.
- [Machines on hc](docs/core.md#creating-terminals-and-agents-machines): how hc reaches core machines.
- [Claude and Codex quotas](docs/quotas.md#claude-and-codex-quotas): remaining usage on every machine and its setup.
- [Pace](docs/quotas.md#pace): Settings › Agents › Pace, when automatic work may start.
- [Notifications](docs/notifications.md#notifications): Web Push and Do not disturb.
- [A default and exceptions](docs/notifications.md#a-default-and-exceptions): one synced policy: a default and its exceptions.
- [Notifications on hc](docs/core.md#notifications): when v3 sends a push, from hc's events.

## Extending and fixing

- [Plugins](docs/plugins.md#wherdr-plugins): optional page plugins and how to install them.
- [The plugin module](docs/plugins.md#the-module): what a plugin file exports.
- [Markers](docs/plugins.md#markers-data-wherdr): `data-wherdr` markers a plugin can find.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#troubleshooting): hc connection, conversations, machines and network problems.
- [Setup on hc](docs/core.md#setup): `HC_SOCKET`, the hc endpoint wherdr talks to.

- [Dictation design](docs/dictation.md): the dictation engines and how to add one.
